threads.thread_goal: Align on target account list and pilot scope for the new device program.

messages.text:
Kicking off the new device education and sales program here. For the first step, we need to lock our pilot scope and target accounts so we can move fast on materials and webinars.

I have started the Target Account Segmentation Sheet in A1 based on our current territories and top prescribing centers, and linked it to T1. Right now it includes hospitals and larger clinics where we already have relationships, grouped by region and specialty, with a draft priority tier.

Can everyone take a look and comment on:
- Any missing key accounts in your area
- Accounts that should move up or down in priority
- How many accounts we think is realistic for the first pilot wave, given the 21-day timeline

Please add comments directly in A1 and reply here with any major changes you propose so we can converge quickly.

Thanks for setting this up. I have gone through A1 and added a couple of regional clinics that send a lot of referrals but were not on the list yet.

I also suggested moving two community hospitals from tier 3 to tier 2 because they have been asking about similar devices recently.

For the pilot wave size, my first thought is around 10 to 12 accounts so we can manage follow-up and logging properly, but I am open to adjusting once we hear from everyone.

I had a quick look at A1 and added one private clinic I work with a lot. Not sure if it fits the criteria for the pilot, but they are usually open to trying new devices.

I did not change any tiers yet because I am not fully sure how we are ranking them. Could someone clarify if we are prioritising by current volume, potential, or just existing relationship?

Good question. For the tiers in A1, I used a mix of:
- Current procedure volume where the device is relevant
- Openness to education programs (based on past events)
- Strategic importance for the region

Existing relationship is a factor but not the only one. If you think that private clinic has strong potential and is usually responsive to training, it could be a tier 2 candidate. Maybe add a comment in the sheet with a short justification and we can review together.

I have reviewed my region in A1 and added two teaching hospitals that are strong candidates for education-led adoption. I also moved one existing account from tier 1 to tier 2 because their current volume is lower and they are slower to adopt new tech.

On pilot size, I would lean closer to 12 to 15 accounts so we get a better spread across specialties, but we should make sure we can support webinars and follow-up for all of them within the 21 days.

I have gone through A1 as well, mainly checking alignment with where we can realistically run educational sessions in the next three weeks.

From a training logistics point of view, a first wave of around 12 accounts feels manageable if we cluster them by region and specialty. That would also give us enough variation to test the educational slide deck and webinar format.

Once we agree on the final list and tiers, I will use A1 as the base for planning T7 (pilot webinars) and aligning with the educational slide deck in A2.

I added a comment in A1 for that private clinic with some context on their case mix and interest in similar devices.

If we are aiming for around 12 accounts, should we try to balance between hospitals and clinics, or focus mainly on hospitals for the first wave?

My view is that for the first wave we should focus mostly on hospitals, especially those with teaching programs, because they tend to engage more with structured education.

Maybe we can include a small number of high-potential clinics, like the one you mentioned, but keep the majority as hospitals so the educational webinars and materials are easier to standardise.

Agree with focusing on hospitals for the first wave. Looking at A1, we could structure it as:
- 8 to 9 hospitals (mix of teaching and high-volume centers)
- 3 to 4 clinics that are very engaged and easy to reach

That would still give us a good test of the program while keeping the educational logistics under control.

Thanks everyone for the updates in A1. I have gone through the comments and proposed tier changes and made the following adjustments:
- Confirmed the two new teaching hospitals as tier 1
- Kept the slower adopter hospital at tier 2
- Marked three high-potential clinics as tier 2, others as tier 3 for now

This gives us 14 tier 1 and tier 2 accounts that look suitable for the pilot.

Proposal: we set the first pilot wave at 14 accounts, mostly hospitals with a few key clinics, and treat the remaining tier 3 accounts as a second wave after we review pilot results.

From the education side, 14 accounts is workable if we cluster webinars and use the same core content from A2. It also gives us enough data points for the KPI tracking in A6 later.

I support the proposal: 14 accounts in the first wave, with the rest as a follow-up wave after we complete the pilot review.

Works for me. Having 14 accounts in the first wave should give us a good mix of feedback for T8 later on.

I will make sure my accounts in A1 are correctly tagged and that I am ready to log all interactions in line with the CRM process once we finalise it.

I am ok with 14 accounts as well. I will focus on the two clinics and one hospital in my area that are now marked as tier 1 or 2 in A1.

Please let me know if there is any specific info we need to capture from these accounts beyond the standard CRM fields once T10 is defined.

I am aligned with the 14-account pilot wave and the tiering you proposed in A1. This gives us a clear focus and should help us avoid spreading the educational resources too thin.

Once we see how engagement looks in the first two weeks, we can decide if any tier 3 accounts should be moved up for the second wave.

Great, sounds like we have convergence.

To summarise:
- A1 now contains the agreed list of pilot accounts, with tiers updated based on everyone s input
- We will include 14 accounts in the first pilot wave, mostly hospitals plus a few high-potential clinics
- Remaining tier 3 accounts will be considered for a second wave after the pilot review

Unless there are objections by end of day, I will mark T1 as complete and treat the current version of A1 as our approved pilot account list and tiering.
No objections from my side. I will start mapping these 14 accounts in A1 to potential webinar slots for T7 and align the educational content plan accordingly.
All good for me as well. I will prepare outreach for my assigned accounts based on the agreed tiers in A1 and wait for the final script from A3 before scheduling detailed calls.
No objections here. I will focus on the three pilot accounts assigned to me in A1 and get ready to log all interactions once we confirm the CRM process.

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise educational slide deck and sales script.

messages.text:
I have uploaded the first draft of the clinician-focused educational slide deck as A2, linked to T2.

Structure so far:
- Overview of the condition and current treatment pathway
- Device mechanism and key features
- Indications and contraindications
- Clinical data summary (only approved data)
- Safety information and handling
- Case examples and workflow integration

Can you review A2 with two lenses:
1) Does it support the kind of education-led conversations you want to have in your accounts?
2) Are there any claims or phrases that might be risky from a promotional standpoint, so we can clean them up before regulatory review and T12?

Also, we need to align this with the sales call script and objection guide in A3 (T3). Please share any must-have talking points or common objections you want reflected in both.

Thanks for pulling this together. I have gone through A2 and added comments on a few slides:
- Suggested simplifying some of the mechanism diagrams so they are easier to explain in a short visit
- Flagged one phrase that could be interpreted as a superiority claim vs competitors; we should probably reword that to focus on features and approved outcomes only

For A3 and T3, I propose the script follows this flow:
1) Short context on the condition and unmet need
2) Brief intro of the device and how it fits into current workflow
3) Two or three key benefits tied to clinical practice (not just technical specs)
4) Safety and contraindications
5) Close with next step: demo, trial, or educational session invite

Common objections we should cover: budget constraints, learning curve, and concerns about procedure time.

I reviewed A2 as well. The clinical data slides look solid and not overloaded, which will help in conversations.

One question: on the case example slide, we mention a reduction in procedure time. Is that based on approved data, or is it more anecdotal? I want to be sure we do not overstate anything when we talk to clinicians.

For A3, I would like to see a clear way to transition from the educational part to discussing next steps, so it does not feel like a hard switch to selling.

I went through A2 quickly. It looks very detailed, which is good, but I am not sure how much of it we should use in a short in-person visit versus a webinar.

Would it make sense to have a shorter version or a few key slides that we can use as a leave-behind or quick overview, and keep the full deck for webinars?

I added some comments in A2 on the benefits section to make the language more practical for day-to-day use, focusing on workflow and patient selection.

For A3 and T3, I suggest we include a short checklist at the end of the script that reminds us to confirm indications, contraindications, and to avoid any off-label discussion. That will also make it easier to align with the compliance checklist in A5 later.

Good catch on the procedure time point. The reduction mentioned in A2 is based on a small subset of the approved clinical data, but the way it is currently phrased could sound broader than what is documented.

I will adjust that slide to:
- Clearly state the sample size and study context
- Use more neutral wording, focusing on observed trends rather than promises

This should make it easier for regulatory to approve during T12 and keep our conversations safe.

On the length of A2: I agree that we need two modes.

Proposal:
- Full deck for webinars and scheduled educational sessions
- A shorter subset of 6 to 8 slides for in-person visits, aligned with the quick-reference sheet in T5

I can mark the core slides in A2 that should be used for the shorter version, and we can mirror those key points in A3 so the script stays consistent.

I like that approach. If we align the shorter version of A2 with the one-page sheet from T5 and the script in A3, it will make it much easier for us to stay on message.

For the script structure in A3, I drafted an outline in the doc:
- Opening: confirm time and focus on education
- Needs assessment: ask about current workflow and pain points
- Key messages: 3 main benefits, each tied to a clinical scenario
- Safety and contraindications
- Close: propose next step (webinar, demo, or trial)

Can everyone check that outline and suggest any missing elements before we send A2 and A3 for regulatory review under T12?

The outline in A3 looks good to me. One thing I would add is a short section on handling questions about competing devices without making direct comparisons that could be problematic.

Maybe we can include a standard way to respond, focusing on our device s approved indications and features, and then redirecting away from detailed competitor discussion.

I added a section in A3 for common objections, starting with:
- Budget and reimbursement
- Learning curve and training time
- Concerns about complications

For each, I drafted responses that stay within approved claims and point back to the clinical data in A2. We should have regulatory double-check these during T12, but the structure should be ready.

I reviewed the outline in A3 and added a note asking for a simple transition phrase from the educational part to the next steps, so it feels natural.

Also, could we include one or two example questions we can ask to check understanding before we move to closing?

I have incorporated your suggestions into A3:
- Added a short section on how to respond when clinicians ask about other devices, focusing on our approved indications and avoiding direct comparisons
- Included two example questions to check understanding before closing, as requested

I also cleaned up the language in A2 to remove any implied superiority claims and made sure all clinical statements are tied to referenced data.

From my side, the structure and key messages of A2 are now consistent and ready for regulatory review.

Thanks for the updates. I have done a final pass on A3 and it now covers:
- Clear opening and needs assessment
- Three core messages aligned with A2
- Safety and contraindications
- Standard responses to top objections
- Guidance on competitor questions
- Close with next steps

From a field perspective, this is usable for the pilot as long as regulatory signs off. I suggest we treat this version of A3 as our standard script and objection guide for the pilot and route both A2 and A3 through regulatory under T12.

Aligned from my side. The script in A3 feels practical and the objection responses are clear enough to use in calls.

Once regulatory comes back with any edits via T12, we should post a short summary of changes so everyone knows what to adjust.

I am comfortable using the current A3 for the pilot once it is approved. The example questions and transition phrases help a lot.

Please just let us know when the final version is ready so I do not accidentally use an outdated script.

Same here. The alignment between A2 and A3 looks good, and the structure should make it easier to keep conversations compliant.

Once regulatory feedback is in, I can help with T12 to implement any requested changes and post a brief change log in the channel.

threads.thread_goal: Lock the digital outreach plan and webinar schedule.

messages.text:
Building on the approved pilot account list in A1, I have drafted a digital outreach plan as A4, linked to T4, and a first pass at the pilot webinar schedule for T7.

Proposal for digital channels and content types in A4:
- Email: invitation to webinars, follow-up with A2 highlights, and links to approved materials
- Professional social media (for example, clinician-focused platforms): short educational posts pointing to webinars and on-demand content
- No direct-to-patient channels for this pilot

For T7, I have outlined 4 pilot webinars:
1) Intro to the device and indications (multi-center)
2) Workflow integration and case discussions
3) Safety, contraindications, and risk management
4) Q and A session after initial use

Each webinar is mapped to a subset of the 14 pilot accounts in A1.

Please review A4 and the T7 schedule and share feedback on:
- Channels we should add or remove
- Whether the topics and timing work for your accounts
- Any constraints we should consider for invitations and follow-up.

Thanks for putting this together. Looking at A4, the email plus professional social media mix makes sense for our audience.

For my accounts in A1, early mornings or late afternoons tend to work best for webinars. I added comments in T7 suggesting time windows for each cluster.

One question: do we plan to record the webinars and share on-demand links, or keep them live only for the pilot?

I reviewed A4 and the T7 outline. For my region, email is definitely the primary channel. Some clinicians also follow our professional social media, but they usually respond better to direct invitations.

I added a note in A4 suggesting that we send a short reminder email the day before each webinar, with the key learning objectives listed clearly.

I had a look at A4. It looks good, but I am not sure how much I should be involved in posting on social media versus just sharing the official posts.

Could we clarify in A4 whether the marketing team will handle posting and we just share links with our contacts, or if we are expected to post from our own profiles as well?

From my side, the four webinar topics in T7 cover the main areas we need. For a couple of teaching hospitals in A1, evenings might work better than mornings, so I added that note in the schedule.

On channels, I agree we should avoid any direct-to-patient outreach. Keeping it to email and professional platforms is safer and more targeted.

On recording: my suggestion is that we record all webinars and make on-demand versions available only to HCPs from the pilot accounts, using a gated link.

This would:
- Help those who cannot attend live
- Give us more touchpoints for follow-up emails in A4

We just need to ensure that the recordings use only approved content from A2 and that any live Q and A is moderated to avoid off-label discussion.

On social media responsibilities: the plan in A4 assumes that marketing will publish the official posts on our corporate channels, and we as a team can share or forward those links to our contacts.

I will add a note in A4 to make that explicit, so no one feels they need to create their own posts, which could create compliance risks.

Recording the webinars and using gated links sounds good to me, as long as the content is fully aligned with A2 and approved.

For the pilot, I suggest we stick to:
- Email as the primary channel for invitations and reminders
- Professional social media as a secondary channel, with posts managed by marketing

I do not see a need to add more channels at this stage, given the timeline.

I agree with that channel mix. Email plus professional social media is enough for the pilot, and it keeps things simple.

For T7, the proposed four webinars work for my accounts as long as we can offer at least one early morning and one late afternoon slot. I added preferences in the schedule.

Thanks for clarifying. I am comfortable sharing the official posts from marketing and focusing my effort on direct email invitations.

The four webinar topics in T7 look good to me. I just added a note that one of my clinics prefers lunchtime sessions if possible.

Channel selection and the recording plan work for me as well. Keeping it focused will help us measure impact more clearly in A6 later.

On the schedule in T7, I think we can lock the topics as proposed. The main open point is final dates and times per region, which we can now confirm based on everyone s comments.

Based on the preferences you all added to T7, here is a consolidated proposal:
- Webinar 1: next Tuesday, 8:00 to 9:00, covering 6 hospitals
- Webinar 2: next Thursday, 17:00 to 18:00, covering 4 hospitals and 2 clinics
- Webinar 3: following Monday, 12:30 to 13:15, focused on safety and contraindications
- Webinar 4: following Thursday, 17:00 to 18:00, open Q and A for all pilot accounts

Each pilot account in A1 is mapped to at least one webinar, with some invited to two.

If there are no major conflicts, I will treat these dates and topics as final for T7 and update A4 with the confirmed schedule for email and social posts.

Those dates and times work for my accounts. I will start pre-warning key contacts so they can block their calendars before the official invites go out.

From my side, we can consider the webinar topics and schedule in T7 confirmed for the pilot.

No conflicts on my side either. The early morning and late afternoon slots cover my main hospitals well.

I will coordinate with my contacts and highlight the safety-focused webinar, since that is usually a key concern.

The lunchtime session is perfect for my clinic, thanks for including that.

I am ok with this schedule and will wait for the final invite templates from A4 before sending anything out.

All good from my side as well. With channels and schedule now aligned, we should be ready to move T4 and T7 forward.

Once the invite templates are final in A4, I can help test the first batch of emails with a small group of contacts to check deliverability and interest.

threads.thread_goal: Align on CRM logging, KPIs and reporting expectations.

messages.text:
I have created the KPI tracking template as A6, linked to T6, and drafted a CRM logging guideline as A8, aligned with A5.

In A6, the main KPIs for the pilot are:
- Number of HCPs invited
- Webinar registrations and attendance
- Number of demos requested
- Number of trial starts
- Orders placed

Each row includes fields for account, contact, stage, estimated value, and next step.

In A8, I outlined the minimum data to log in the CRM for each interaction related to the new device.

Please review A6 and A8 and share:
- Any KPIs you think we are missing or could simplify
- Whether the CRM fields and process in T10 are realistic for your day-to-day work
- Any concerns about double entry or extra admin load.

Thanks for setting this up. A6 looks clear and not too heavy.

I suggest we add one more field: source of engagement (webinar, in-person visit, email only), so we can see which activities are driving demos and orders.

On A8 and T10, the required fields per interaction seem reasonable. My only concern is making sure we do not have to enter the same information in both A6 and the CRM. Ideally, A6 should pull from CRM data or be used only for summary reporting.

I reviewed A6 and A8. The KPIs make sense and match what we usually track.

For T10, I added a comment suggesting that we predefine a new device-specific activity type in the CRM, so we can filter interactions easily later.

I am ok with the minimum data set per interaction, as long as we keep notes short and focused on key questions and next steps.

I had a look at A6. It is helpful, but I am a bit worried about remembering all the fields after each call.

Would it be possible to have a very short checklist or quick reference (maybe linked to A5) that we can keep open during calls, so we do not forget to log the key items in the CRM?

I added a couple of suggestions in A6:
- Separate demos requested from demos completed
- Add a simple field for feedback category (clinical, workflow, pricing, other) to help with T8 later

On A8, I think the process is workable. We just need to be clear that every interaction related to the new device must be logged, even if it is a short follow-up email.

Good points. I have updated A6 to:
- Add a field for engagement source (webinar, visit, email)
- Split demos into requested and completed
- Include a feedback category field as suggested

On the double entry concern: the idea is that CRM remains the primary system of record, and A6 is a reporting view. I will coordinate with the CRM admin so we can export the relevant fields into A6 periodically, rather than asking you to maintain both manually.

On the quick reference: we can extend A5 to include a short section on CRM logging for the new device.

I will add a one-page summary linked from A5 that lists the minimum fields to capture after each interaction, matching A8 and T10. That way you can keep it open during calls as a reminder.

With those updates, the KPI set in A6 looks complete but still manageable.

For the pilot, I suggest we lock the KPIs as:
- Invitations, registrations, attendance
- Demos requested and completed
- Trials started
- Orders placed
- Feedback category

If everyone agrees, we can treat this as the final KPI set for T6.

I am aligned with that KPI list. It covers the full funnel without adding too many extra fields.

On A8 and T10, I support creating a specific activity type for the new device and making it mandatory to log at least one interaction per active pilot account per week during the pilot.

The idea of a one-page summary linked to A5 will help a lot. With that and the defined KPIs in A6, I feel more confident about logging correctly.

I am ok with the KPI list and the CRM process as long as we get a short walkthrough before the pilot starts.

I agree with locking the KPIs as you summarised. It will also make it easier to compile the post-pilot report in A7 and T11.

For the CRM process in A8 and T10, I propose we define the minimum data per interaction as:
- Account and contact
- Interaction type and date
- Stage (interest, demo, trial, order)
- Short note on key questions or feedback

If we all follow that, we should have enough detail without overloading the system.

I have updated A8 and T10 to reflect that minimum data set and the new device-specific activity type.

To summarise the CRM process for the pilot:
- Every interaction related to the new device is logged with the defined fields
- A6 is populated via CRM exports, not manual double entry
- A5 includes a short reminder checklist for logging

If there are no objections, we can treat this as the agreed CRM logging process and minimum data set for the pilot.

No objections from me. The KPI set in A6 and the CRM process in A8 and T10 are clear.

I suggest we schedule a short internal training under T9 to walk through A6, A8, and A5 before the first webinars, so everyone is comfortable with the process.

All good from my side as well. With A6, A8, and A5 aligned, I think we have enough structure to track the pilot properly.

Looking forward to the walkthrough session so we can clarify any remaining questions live.
I am ok with the final KPIs and CRM process as summarised. The training under T9 will be helpful for me to see examples of good entries in A6 and the CRM.

threads.thread_goal: Share pilot results, feedback and decide on broader rollout.

messages.text:
We have completed the initial pilot period with the 14 accounts in A1. I have compiled the KPI data from A6 and the qualitative feedback into a draft post-pilot report as A7, linked to T11.

Headline numbers from A6:
- 78 HCPs invited, 52 registrations, 41 attendees across 4 webinars
- 19 demos requested, 15 completed
- 9 trial starts
- 4 orders placed so far, with several more in late-stage discussions

A7 also summarises key feedback themes: strong interest in education, questions about workflow integration, and some pricing concerns.

Please review A7 and share:
- Any corrections or missing data from your accounts
- Your view on whether we should expand beyond the initial 14 accounts
- Whether the current sales script in A3 needs adjustments before a broader rollout.

Thanks for pulling the report together. I checked A7 against my notes and A6, and the numbers for my accounts match.

From my perspective, the education-led approach worked well. The main blockers I heard were around internal budget cycles rather than lack of interest.

I think we are ready to expand to a second wave of accounts from A1, especially the tier 2 and some tier 3 sites that showed early curiosity. We should keep the same core script from A3, with maybe a bit more emphasis on workflow and training support.

I reviewed A7 and added a small correction for one of my demos that was completed but logged as requested only in A6. Apart from that, the summary reflects my experience.

Clinicians appreciated the educational webinars and the clarity of the script in A3. The main questions I got were about how to fit the device into existing protocols and how much training the staff would need.

I support expanding to more accounts, but I would like us to refine the script slightly to include a stronger section on implementation support.

I checked A7 and my data is mostly there, but I think one of my trial starts is missing from A6. I will double-check my CRM entries and update if needed.

In terms of feedback, some clinicians liked the educational content but felt the calls were a bit long. Maybe we can tighten the script in A3 for shorter visits, while keeping the full version for webinars.

I have reviewed A7 and the underlying data in A6. The conversion from demos to trials and orders is encouraging for a first pilot.

On the target account strategy, I think we should:
- Keep the 14 pilot accounts as ongoing focus
- Add the remaining tier 2 accounts from A1 to the next wave
- Select a few tier 3 accounts that showed interest during the pilot period

This would expand our reach while still keeping the program manageable.

Thanks for the corrections; I will update A6 and A7 to reflect the additional demo and trial start once your CRM entries are confirmed.

On the script length, we can create two variants of A3:
- A full version for scheduled educational sessions
- A shorter version for quick visits, focusing on the top two benefits and a clear next step

I will draft the shorter variant and mark it clearly in A3 so we do not confuse versions.

I like that expansion plan. It keeps our focus on the accounts most likely to move while giving us more volume for the next phase.

So in practice, that would mean:
- Continue active engagement with the 14 pilot accounts
- Add all remaining tier 2 accounts from A1
- Add 3 to 5 tier 3 accounts that have already shown interest

If we agree, we can update A1 accordingly and treat this as our go-forward target strategy.

I am aligned with that approach. The tier 2 accounts I have in A1 are already asking when they can get more information, so it makes sense to bring them into the program now.

For the script in A3, I would keep the core structure but add a short section that explicitly offers training support and follow-up after the first cases.

I am ok with expanding to more accounts as you described. I will need some guidance on prioritising my time between the original pilot accounts and the new ones, but the updated A1 should help.

On the script, a shorter version will be very helpful for my shorter visits.
I support formalising that as our updated target strategy. I can help update A1 with the new wave of accounts and mark them clearly so we can track adoption over time in A6 and A7.

I have now:
- Updated A6 and A7 with the corrected demo and trial data
- Created a shorter visit-focused variant of the script in A3, keeping the same key messages but trimming some of the detail

Based on the feedback in A7, I also added a small section in both script variants that highlights implementation support and training options.

Please take a quick look at the updated A3 and confirm that it still works for your conversations.

I reviewed the updated A3. Both the full and short versions read well and reflect what we learned during the pilot.

The added emphasis on workflow and training support addresses most of the questions I heard. I am comfortable using this script for a broader rollout.

Same here. The updated A3 captures the main objections and questions we saw in the pilot, and the shorter version will help in busy clinics.

I do not see any issues that would block us from using this script for the next wave of accounts.

I tried the short version of A3 in one visit yesterday and it flowed much better for me. The structure is easy to follow.

I am ok with using this script going forward.

The updated script in A3 looks good and consistent with the findings in A7. I think we can treat this as our standard for the broader rollout.

We should just make sure that any future tweaks are documented and communicated clearly so everyone stays aligned.

Great, thanks for the confirmations.

To summarise where we landed based on A7 and the discussion:
- We will keep the 14 pilot accounts as ongoing focus and expand to additional tier 2 and selected tier 3 accounts in A1
- A1 will be updated to reflect this broader target list
- The updated script in A3, with full and short variants, will be our standard for the broader rollout

I will finalise A7 under T11 with these decisions and share it with the wider stakeholder group.
